name: Sophocles
role: Athenian tragic playwright (c. 496–406 BC), also treasurer, general and commissioner
summary: Sophocles was an Athenian dramatist who also held public office under Pericles and, in 411 BC, sat on the commission of ten that preceded the oligarchic regime of the Four Hundred. No treatise or speech of his own survives; his plays give their positions to characters, so his own views on the test's statements are not recorded.

sources.title: Aristotle, Rhetoric 3.18 (Perseus, Freese translation)
sources.author: Aristotle
sources.usedFor: The oldest account of Sophocles's conduct in 411 BC: he admitted approving the setting up of the Four Hundred, calling it wicked but the best available.

sources.title: Britannica, Sophocles (biography)
sources.author: Britannica
sources.usedFor: His offices: treasurer 442, general 440 and later, proboulos 413; no statement is settled by them.

sources.title: Britannica, Antigone by Sophocles
sources.author: Britannica
sources.usedFor: Scholarly summary of the play, confirming its positions are spoken by characters; settles no statement.

booksNotUsed.reason: Translations of his plays: the words belong to characters, and a character's view is not the playwright's position.

notFound.work: Sophocles's own speeches, letters or political writings
